edits.html: Virilization in a girl: which source? Clitoral enlargement — virilization, which normal adrenarche never causes; at age 10, pubic hair alone would be ordinary · Adrenal marker — DHEAS (dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate) comes almost only from the zona reticularis, the innermost layer of the adrenal cortex; urine 17-ketosteroids rise with it · Ovarian marker — testosterone in a girl comes mostly from the ovary · High DHEAS, normal testosterone, normal pelvic ultrasound — adrenal source · High testosterone with an adnexal mass — androgen-secreting ovarian tumor, such as a Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor · DHEAS far above range in a child — an adrenal tumor until proven otherwise; many pediatric virilizing adrenal tumors are carcinomas, and histology, not labs, separates adenoma from carcinoma · Nonclassic congenital adrenal hyperplasia — the commoner adrenal cause, marked by a high 17-hydroxyprogesterone
edits.note: new angle: localizing an androgen source in a virilized girl

edits.html: How NBME framed it The lead-in asks only for a diagnosis, and the decider sits in one sentence of labs with reference ranges: DHEAS (dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate) is high while testosterone is normal. Three options are adenomas at the adrenal, ovary and pituitary, making it a location question; androgen insensitivity and polycystic ovarian syndrome fill the list.

edits.anchor: not large truncal patches, and there is no precocious puberty
edits.html:
True-fact-wrong-slotAndrogen insensitivity syndrome: tempts as an androgen disorder in a genital-examination stem; it is a receptor defect in a 46,XY child with no androgen effect, so it cannot cause clitoromegaly or hirsutism
Unchecked attributeOvarian adenoma: tempts as a virilizing tumor in a girl; an androgen-secreting ovarian tumor raises testosterone, and here testosterone is normal and the pelvic ultrasound shows no mass
Class-vs-memberPituitary adenoma: tempts as the third adenoma and a pituitary cause of precocity; there is no headache or visual field loss, and pituitary adenomas rarely virilize
Unchecked attributePolycystic ovarian syndrome: tempts with hirsutism and acne; testosterone and ovaries are normal, weight is at the 50th percentile, and it does not cause clitoromegaly
